scope: Working local customer journey recommendation engine, not a production deployment.
runtime: Python 3.10+ standard library; verified with Python 3.13.15.

interfaces.cli_success: JSON recommendation object to stdout, exit code 0.
interfaces.cli_invalid_input: JSON error object to stderr, exit code 2. Argument usage errors use argparse's stderr format.
interfaces.python: recommend(payload, explanation_callback=None) -> JSON-compatible dict; invalid input raises ValidationError.
interfaces.callback: Optional injected callable receives a deep copy of the recommendation result and returns {explanations: [{action_id: string, text: string}]}. Only unique action IDs appearing in next_actions or two_step_plan are accepted. Any invalid entry or callback exception rejects the whole supplement, preserving deterministic recommendations. No callback is configured or invoked by the CLI.

journey.stages: Nonempty list of {id: nonempty string, name: nonempty string, prerequisites?: stage ID list}. Every stage must have at least one action.
journey.actions: Nonempty list of {id: nonempty string, name: nonempty string, stage_id: stage ID, prerequisites?: action ID list, tags?: string list, priority?: finite number in [-1000000, 1000000]}.

user.completed_stages: Required list of known stage IDs.
user.completed_actions: Optional list of known action IDs; defaults to empty.
user.preferences: Optional list of preferred tags; defaults to empty.
user.excluded_actions: Optional list of known action IDs; defaults to empty.
user.excluded_tags: Optional list of disallowed tags; defaults to empty.

input_schema.validation: Unknown fields, duplicate IDs/list values/JSON keys, invalid types, invalid references, stage cycles, action cycles and mixed stage/action cycles are rejected. Tags are free-form case-sensitive strings; unfamiliar preference tags are allowed.

semantics.eligibility: An incomplete action must not be excluded by ID or tag; all its prerequisite actions and its stage's prerequisite stages must be completed.
semantics.completion: Completed stage snapshots are authoritative and imply completion of all their actions. Otherwise a stage completes once all its actions and all prerequisite stages complete. All configured actions are required, not alternative branches.
semantics.ranking: score = priority (default 0) + 10 * count(matching preference tags); descending score, then ascending case-sensitive action ID. This is an explicit policy score, not a probability, rating or learned prediction.
semantics.plan: Greedy up to two actions. Simulate completion of the first action, recompute stage completion and eligibility, then select the next highest-ranked action. Step two is conditional on successful completion of prior plan actions; it is not asserted to be currently eligible.
semantics.explanations: Each recommended action includes satisfied prerequisite stage/action IDs and a deterministic explanation; plan entries identify assumed completed prior plan actions.
semantics.impossible_progression: Fixed-point reachability with current exclusions determines whether every stage can eventually complete. A ready journey may still have progression_possible=false when a later required action is excluded.
semantics.status: completed if all stages are complete; ready if any next action is eligible; blocked otherwise.

limitations: Local JSON-file input and JSON stdout only; no database, web UI, authentication, event tracking or action execution.
No network, provider calls, dependencies, training, financial estimates or token estimates.
No global plan optimization, optional action branches, durations, budgets or competing resource constraints.
User completion snapshots are trusted historical facts; contradictory historical completion order is not rejected.

Callback structured action IDs are validated; arbitrary explanatory prose is not fact-checked and must be treated as untrusted text. Callback availability, latency and side effects are the caller's responsibility.
Fixed-point simulation is intended for modest local journey configurations, with no large-scale performance claim.
Tests use labeled synthetic fixtures, not measured customer conversion outcomes.

coverage: eligible actions, weighted preferences, exclusions, completed journeys
two-step conditional planning and prerequisite explanations
deterministic ties independent of declaration order
impossible future progression and excluded descendants
invalid references, schema, numeric priorities and cycles
callback acceptance, invented IDs, nonrecommended IDs, malformed output, exceptions and mutation isolation
duplicate JSON keys and subprocess CLI success/error
